title: AICPA & CIMA AI topic page: an error page, not guidance
answer: This is the AICPA & CIMA technology topic page for artificial intelligence, harvested on 26 September 2026, and it does not load. The URL returns a not found message with a link back to the homepage. The only substantive text is the organisation's boilerplate description of itself as the most influential body of accountants and finance experts, with 689,000 members, students and engaged professionals globally. It contains no audit use cases, no risk guidance and no assurance positions, so the claim it is cited for is not supported by this capture.

sections.body: It is a page on the AICPA & CIMA website, filed under the technology topic and titled for artificial intelligence. The publisher is AICPA & CIMA, and the site is presented by the Association of International Certified Professional Accountants, founded by the American Institute of CPAs and The Chartered Institute of Management Accountants. The intended scope, judging by the URL, is an AI resource line for the accounting profession. What was actually harvested on 26 September 2026 is not that resource. It is the site's not found page, carrying only the organisation's standard header and footer text. No publication date, author or document type is stated for the AI material itself.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The captured text is an error page. It states twice that the page cannot be found and offers a button to return to the homepage. Around that message sits the site's standard framing. The header describes AICPA & CIMA as the most influential body of accountants and finance experts in the world, with 689,000 members, students and engaged professionals globally, and says it advocates for the profession, the public interest and business sustainability. The footer says the site is brought to you by the Association of International Certified Professional Accountants, described as the global voice of the accounting and finance profession, founded by the American Institute of CPAs and The Chartered Institute of Management Accountants. There is no artificial intelligence content of any kind. The capture contains no discussion of audit use, risk, assurance, governance, standards, tools or adoption. Nothing indicates what the intended page covered, when it was published, or whether it has been moved or replaced. A reader looking for the profession's position on AI in accounting will not find it here.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The only figure given is 689,000 members, students and engaged professionals globally, from the AICPA & CIMA header. The text also claims the body is the most influential of accountants and finance experts in the world, and names the American Institute of CPAs and The Chartered Institute of Management Accountants as founders of the Association. It gives no AI-related numbers, definitions or positions.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: As captured, this source cannot support the point it is cited for. It offers no audit use cases, no risk material and no assurance positions, so a reader following AI in accounting gains nothing on those questions from this page. Its only value is confirming that AICPA & CIMA is the publisher behind the intended resource and that it speaks for a very large membership, which matters for authority if a working version of the page is located. Until then the citation should point somewhere that actually loads.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Accounting

sections.body: The capture is a broken link, so it is partial by definition and shows nothing of the intended content. No publication or review date is stated, and no author is named. The text that does appear is institutional self-description rather than professional guidance, and it is promotional in tone. It covers no AI topic at all, and it cannot be used to show what the profession has settled on regarding audit use, risk or assurance.
